title: An inverse planned oil release validation method for estimating oil slick thickness from thermal contrast remote sensing by in-scene calibration
author: Leifer, Melton, et al.
materials: The approach also yields the pixel's fractional water / oil coverage and emulsion level, both of which affect the spectral feature. Emulsions scatter light with a wavelength dependency that significantly alters further the spectral feature's shape. Fortunately, the spectral feature is weakly sensitive to emulsion droplet size [18]. To date, near-infrared hyperspectral oil thickness remote sensing has not been field validated for oil slicks of known thickness. Furthermore, the effect of sub-pixel thickness and emulsion heterogeneity on the derived thickness remains unknown. Currently, commercial near-infrared imaging spectrometers are unavailable.

steps.title: Select target oil segment
steps.instruction: Identify a thick, actionable oil slick segment on the sea surface and coordinate the airborne imaging platform and the two boom vessels so that the airplane can repeatedly image the segment while it is being collected.

steps.title: Deploy and position boom system
steps.instruction: Connect two 33‑m long, 12.5 cm (6 in) diameter harbor booms with two ~10‑m tow ropes to the two fishing boats and to the modified weir skimmer; motor the boom vessels very slowly toward the target segment, towing the skimmer asymmetrically to keep it offset from the boom apex.

substeps.instruction: Maintain a steady, nearly straight line to avoid disturbing the slick or causing entrainment.
Continuously communicate with the airplane and a third off‑load vessel to monitor drift speed and oil entrainment.

steps.title: Close boom and equalize legs
steps.instruction: When the oil accumulates at the boom apex, close the boom mouth, then move the trailing boom vessel forward so the boom legs become symmetric and the skimmer sits at the apex, incorporating air into the slick and stabilising it.

steps.title: Off‑load collected oil
steps.instruction: Open the skimmer latchable door, attach a throttled 160‑gallon min⁻¹ gasoline‑powered water pump to the skimmer port, and pump the oil into 20‑L (5‑gal) sealed plastic buckets; if oil is too viscous to flow, use a pool leaf skimmer to manually transfer it.

substeps.instruction: Seal each bucket and label with time, collect number, and fill order.
Confirm negligible loss by visual monitoring from the sea‑surface observers and later aerial image inspection.

steps.title: Handle collection failure
steps.instruction: If oil leaks from the skimmer, abandon the current collect: release the free side of the boom, have the other boat surge forward with the boom streaming behind, relocate to a new slick segment, and re‑attach the free side to the second boom vessel.

steps.title: Weigh oil samples in laboratory
steps.instruction: Weigh each 5‑gal bucket on an NTEP Ranger 7000 balance (35 kg capacity, 0.5 g readability) and on a Sartorius LC3200D balance (3 kg capacity, 1 mg readability) using Class 1 calibration weights.

steps.title: Determine water fraction by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Subsample each bucket, centrifuge the sample for at least 1 h at 3000 RPM, then measure total sample volume and water volume to quantify emulsion level.

steps.title: Pre‑process INU navigation data
steps.instruction: Correct missing INU position points by linear interpolation of surrounding data, fill time‑base irregularities to a uniform 50 Hz rate, and filter yaw, pitch, and roll with a five‑point (0.1 s) median filter.

steps.title: Project imagery onto uniform grid
steps.instruction: Use the ImGRAFT toolbox in MATLAB 2016a to project TIR and VIS images onto a UTM grid at 0.2 m resolution using 2‑D cubic‑spline interpolation.

steps.title: Determine camera sensor size (FOV)
steps.instruction: In a raw TIR city‑scene image (640 × 480 px), select three distinct landmarks, obtain their pixel coordinates (Iₙ,Jₙ) and corresponding lat/long from Google Earth, and solve for the true sensor dimensions; resulting sensor sizes are 11.69 × 8.80 cm for the A655s TIR camera and 23.43 × 15.00 cm for the 7 K HDPro VIS camera.

steps.title: Optimize camera‑INU alignment
steps.instruction: Run ImGRAFT optimization varying camera sensor size, translation (x,y) and yaw while fixing camera height, pitch = 90° (nadir) and roll = 0°, to align the three ground‑reference points with their GPS coordinates.

steps.title: Apply temporal offset correction
steps.instruction: Determine a temporal offset of 0.1 s between video frames and INU data and a sensor‑size scaling factor of 106 % for both the A655s and 7 K cameras by minimizing RMS error of overlapping projected images.

steps.title: Co‑register TIR and VIS imagery
steps.instruction: Create a DEM (sea‑surface altitude = 0 m), select three non‑collinear control points by matching oil features in TIR and VIS images, and run ImGRAFT to refine TIR camera location, yaw, pitch, roll, and focal length; keep world coordinates and distortion coefficients fixed.

steps.title: Mask and de‑speckle TIR image
steps.instruction: In ImageJ, trace artifacts in the VIS image to create a mask, import the mask to MATLAB and set masked TIR pixels to NaN, then apply imclose.m with a 5 × 5‑pixel structural element and smooth.m to the TIR image.

steps.title: Classify thick‑oil pixels
steps.instruction: Classify pixels as thick oil based on brightness temperature (TB) values and texture; use water aft of the boat stern as the reference TB for oil‑free water.

steps.title: Derive water‑temperature distribution
steps.instruction: Model the TB probability distribution Φ(TB) as the sum of three Gaussians (oil, water, wake) per Eq. (7); identify water pixels where Φ_W > 0.01 a_W, and remove outliers >2 σ from a 1‑m moving average, interpolating their values.

steps.title: Fit background water temperature profile
steps.instruction: Fit non‑outlier water TB values to TB_W(y) = b + c y + sin(d y) (Eq. 8), then construct a piecewise linear background with a Gaussian transition (Eqs. 9‑10) to obtain ΔTB(x,y) = TB(x,y) − TB_W(x,y).

steps.title: Calibrate ΔTB to oil thickness
steps.instruction: Using four successful collects, relate collected oil mass M to ΔTB‑derived area A(ΔTB) with the iterative model M(ΔTB) = k ∫A(ΔTB)dΔTB + N (Eq. 10); start with k = 1, compute k₂ by minimizing N across all collects, and obtain the final calibration curve (Fig. 14).

steps.title: Apply calibration to slick surveys
steps.instruction: For each survey image, compute ΔTB, convert to oil mass using the calibration function, and estimate uncertainties by 10 000 Monte‑Carlo simulations using a TB standard deviation of 0.084 K; fit the resulting mass distribution with a Gaussian and report the half‑width as the uncertainty.
